entities.summary:
The Battle of Kleidion was a pivotal event in the Byzantine-Bulgarian Wars. It took place on July 29, 1014, in the Belasica Mountains, marking a significant turning point in the war. The Byzantine Empire, led by Emperor Basil II, delivered a crushing defeat to the Bulgarian army, led by Tsar Samuel. The victory allowed the Byzantines to regain control over key territories in the region, ultimately leading to the decline of the Bulgarian Empire.

The battle was a testament to the military prowess of the Byzantine Empire, which had been making significant strides in recent years. Basil II's tactical genius and the bravery of his soldiers played a crucial role in securing the victory. The battle of Kleidion also had a lasting impact on the region, shaping the course of medieval history in the Balkans.

The legacy of the Battle of Kleidion can still be seen in the modern-day borders and politics of the region. The battle marked the beginning of a long period of Byzantine dominance in the Balkans, which would last for centuries. Despite this, the Bulgarian people would eventually rise again, playing a significant role in the region's history.

As the great Byzantine historian, Michael Attaleiates, once wrote, 'The victory at Kleidion was a triumph not only for the Byzantine Empire, but for the very concept of civilization itself.'
